name: Contextual Modulation
description: Surround effects on neural responses: activity in the receptive field surround modulates central responses. Implements contrastive coding and figure-ground separation. Related to divisive normalization but distinct in spatial structure.
key_references: Schwartz, O., Sejnowski, T. J., & Dayan, P. (2007). Perceptual learning: gain up and down. Current Opinion in Neurobiology, 17(4), 457-462.

Levick, W. R., Oyster, C. K., & Davis, D. L. (1965). Evidence that the lateral geniculate nucleus of the cat does not enforce the lincoln transmission of retinal signals. Brain Research, 1(2), 226-243.
empirical_evidence: Documented extensively in V1, V2, and MT. Surround suppression predicts illusory motion and tilt illusions. Beyond V1, properties become task-dependent and learned. Computational models using normalization explain many properties. Mechanism unclear: could be lateral inhibition, feedback, or normalization.
